matches.text: Quick reference The fixed scalar reference Terms for interpreting the tiny decoder's input identity, regression evidence, replay and checkpoint limits. Bitwise training replay A separately executed repeat of the same frozen training schedule that matches recorded training behavior and state bit for bit within this execution; it is not an independent seed sample or a measurement of variation across seeds. Cached generation agreement Agreement between the KV-cached and complete-prefix paths on generated tokens, decisions and RNG state for the fixed prompt and sampling settings, not proof of useful language quality. Checkpoint round trip Saving and loading persisted decoder, optimizer and tokenizer state exactly, with a fixed logit probe. This narrow check does not establish complete job resumption. Fixed-fixture regression evidence A known result reproduced on unchanged data to detect changed behavior, rather than an independent estimate of generalization. Overlapping window-target slot One target position inside one causal window. Overlapping windows can score the same within-document transition occurrence repeatedly; this reference scores 1,744 slots representing 442 occurrences. Reference input identity The digest binding the tiny decoder configuration, exact corpus and split bytes, and verified scalar-reference source. It identifies inputs, not model capability. Scalar reference decoder The completed first course's 1,188-parameter CPU decoder, used unchanged as a fixed comparison point while the separate practical copy evolves.

Decontamination Check and exclude training overlap with declared protected evaluation material using a specified method. Passing that check does not establish absence of every possible leak. Document occurrence One stored instance of a document. Two records containing the same text are two occurrences and can give that text extra training weight. Exact deduplication Remove repeated text under a declared equality policy. The NeMo example groups text hashes and keeps one representative; it does not detect paraphrases or certify collision-proof equality. Held-out split Validation or test documents kept out of tokenizer learning and model fitting. Validation informs setting choices; test evaluation is reserved for the final assessment. Near-duplicate A document sufficiently similar to another under a declared matching method. Approximate searches can miss related text or group text that should remain distinct. Prepared-document interchange UTF-8 JSONL records with nonblank string id and text fields and retained metadata. Rust loads the supplied selection without redoing filtering, duplicate removal or split assignment. Retention fraction Prepared-document count divided by input-document count for a nonempty input. It measures how much the declared pipeline retains, not the quality of its survivors. Source group Records declared to belong to one related source family. The exercise assigns each supplied group to a single split; that assignment does not prove all related records were discovered. Training corpus The selected documents that supply examples for tokenizer learning and model training, together with evidence of their source and preparation policy.

matches.text: Quick reference The fixed scalar reference Terms for interpreting the tiny decoder's input identity, regression evidence, replay and checkpoint limits. Bitwise training replay A separately executed repeat of the same frozen training schedule that matches recorded training behavior and state bit for bit within this execution; it is not an independent seed sample or a measurement of variation across seeds. Cached generation agreement Agreement between the KV-cached and complete-prefix paths on generated tokens, decisions and RNG state for the fixed prompt and sampling settings, not proof of useful language quality. Checkpoint round trip Saving and loading persisted decoder, optimizer and tokenizer state exactly, with a fixed logit probe. This narrow check does not establish complete job resumption. Fixed-fixture regression evidence A known result reproduced on unchanged data to detect changed behavior, rather than an independent estimate of generalization. Overlapping window-target slot One target position inside one causal window. Overlapping windows can score the same within-document transition occurrence repeatedly; this reference scores 1,744 slots representing 442 occurrences. Reference input identity The digest binding the tiny decoder configuration, exact corpus and split bytes, and verified scalar-reference source. It identifies inputs, not model capability. Scalar reference decoder The completed first course's 1,188-parameter CPU decoder, used unchanged as a fixed comparison point while the separate practical copy evolves.

matches.text: Quick reference Corpus preparation Terms for selecting training text, handling repeated examples, protecting evaluation roles and reading prepared documents. Decontamination Check and exclude training overlap with declared protected evaluation material using a specified method. Passing that check does not establish absence of every possible leak. Document occurrence One stored instance of a document. Two records containing the same text are two occurrences and can give that text extra training weight. Exact deduplication Remove repeated text under a declared equality policy. The NeMo example groups text hashes and keeps one representative; it does not detect paraphrases or certify collision-proof equality. Held-out split Validation or test documents kept out of tokenizer learning and model fitting. Validation informs setting choices; test evaluation is reserved for the final assessment. Near-duplicate A document sufficiently similar to another under a declared matching method. Approximate searches can miss related text or group text that should remain distinct. Prepared-document interchange UTF-8 JSONL records with nonblank string id and text fields and retained metadata. Rust loads the supplied selection without redoing filtering, duplicate removal or split assignment. Retention fraction Prepared-document count divided by input-document count for a nonempty input. It measures how much the declared pipeline retains, not the quality of its survivors. Source group Records declared to belong to one related source family. The exercise assigns each supplied group to a single split; that assignment does not prove all related records were discovered. Training corpus The selected documents that supply examples for tokenizer learning and model training, together with evidence of their source and preparation policy.
